transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in today?

I just have this unbelievable, overwhelming energy and I haven't been able to sit still for over a year now! One minute I'm absolutely thrilled and on top of the world, and the next I'm incredibly irritated and snapping at everyone. I just need to keep moving, so can we speed this up?
Have you ever had a period of at least one week where your mood was extremely elevated or irritable and you had more energy or needed less sleep, not just brief ups and downs?

Yes, absolutely, and it has actually lasted for a really long time now—about a year and two months. During this whole period, I've felt incredibly energetic, constantly on the go, and unable to slow down. My mood just swings wildly between feeling totally euphoric and getting extremely irritated at the slightest things.

latest_inference.note: Previously the candidates were ["Bipolar I Disorder", "Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)"], but based on this conversation, ADHD (Combined Presentation) is less likely because the patient describes a sustained period of elevated/irritable mood with increased energy lasting over a year, which aligns more strongly with a manic episode seen in Bipolar I Disorder. The duration and severity of symptoms, including marked mood swings between euphoria and irritability, are more characteristic of mania than ADHD. Therefore, the current candidate is now solely Bipolar I Disorder.

These symptoms suggest a possible bipolar disorder, particularly Bipolar I Disorder, given the presence of elevated mood and irritability consistent with manic episodes. However, the chronic nature of the symptoms and persistent restlessness also raise the possibility of ADHD, particularly the combined presentation. Previous candidates are not available, so this is the initial formulation.
